label: copy-phase fed-back z, mid-copy (recall_idx 3-5) in long sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase and only when the input token is z, i.e. the model is echoing back an original z (in_tok z holds 100% of activation mass; never fires in the original or delimiter phases or on any other input). Activity sits mid-copy: recall_idx 4 holds ~73% of mass (z was original position 3), with 3 and 5 most of the rest, and L=9 holds 80% of mass (none for L<=6). The strongest examples are L=9 sequences where z is original token 3, often after m (top: 0 o m z f y y v y), and often with y later in the sequence. These are necessary conditions, not sufficient: the feature fires on only ~1.6% of steps matching the predicate (even the L=9, recall_idx 4 case is ~6%), and conditioning on prev_tok m or y in the sequence raises precision only to ~10% while losing most recall. So the trigger is clear (fed-back z in the middle of a long copy), but what picks out the few cases that fire was not found.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=z (+3.85), phase=2 & out_tok=e (+2.53), in_tok=z (+2.50), orig6=y (+2.28), prev_tok=m (+2.09), orig7=y (+2.06). Lower it: orig6=- (-1.74), orig8=- (-1.67), recall_idx=2 (-1.29), prev2_tok=<DEL> (-1.29).
